text:
maria: Quick question for the group: what's our preferred pattern for onboarding tenants into the new isolated-controlplane model? specifically re: peering vs per-tenant endpoints for small customers.
tony: short answer: prefer per-tenant endpoints for security, but peering is cheaper for low-tier where we can't justify ENI+EIP costs.
priya: agree with tony. we should codify a tiered policy: high-tier -> dedicated ENI + optional EIP, mid-tier -> shared per-region relay with per-tenant ACLs, low-tier -> multi-tenant shared endpoint.
maria: ok. how do we handle controlplane auth when switching between models? e.g., session tokens bound to endpoint ip today.
sam: we should stop binding tokens to IP. long-term fix: token binding to tenant-id + session nonce validated by cp. short-term: maintain a mapping service that translates old-binding checks to new semantics.
priya: mapping service idea: controlplane exposes a tenant-ip registry. when we provision peering or ENI we write entries there. validation flow: incoming conn -> lookup tenant id for src ip -> accept if match. this keeps backward compat during migration.
ton y: spelling nit: tony* :) also: peering lifecycle ops are heavy; we need automation to create/delete peering connections, manage route tables, and handle concurrent attachments across accounts.
maria: good call. we also need to measure time to create peering vs attach ENI in worst-case region. worry about migration windows getting long.
sam: rough numbers from last spike: ENI + EIP attach ~2-3m, route table update + propagation ~30-90s, peering + route propagation ~4-6m. plus acceptance delays if cross-account.
priya: implication: for bulk migrations (hundreds of tenants) we must parallelize but stagger to avoid route table limits and AWS API throttles. also track per-AZ limits for ENIs.
ton y: tradeoff doc draft: include cost matrix (monthly infra + ops time) vs security posture vs failover complexity. also enumerate failure modes: incomplete route propagation, SG misconfig, peering auth rejected.
maria: any thoughts on DNS TTL strategy? we don't want long TTLs blocking rapid rollback, but short TTLs increase DNS query volume.
sam: propose 60s TTL during cutover window, revert to 300s steady-state. publish a DNS cutover playbook.
priya: add to playbook: preflight checks: 1) quota checks for ENIs/EIPs in target accounts 2) peering acceptance pre-approvals for cross-account 3) route-table free entry slots 4) security group probe allow rules.
ton y: and add a post-cutover reconciliation: run an automated probe for 1h, and a drift-detector that alerts if any tenant still routes through old path.
devops-bot: infra-task queued: cp-migration-automation -> create-eni-and-register (batch) will run in dry-run mode at 02:00 UTC.
maria: excellent. one more: billing tags must be attached to ENIs/peers for chargeback and seat-level cost reports. sam, can you add this to the migration API?
sam: yup will add tagging + write to tenant-migration-log. also will surface a "migration-cost-estimate" in dry-run output.
priya: i'll collate into a runbook and RFC update. will include sample awscli snippets and the DNS migration checklist.
priya: sample awscli snippet for preflight ENI quota:
```
aws ec2 describe-account-attributes --attribute-names max-instances-per-region
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=subnet-id,Values=..." | jq '.Reservations | length'
```
maria: thanks everyone. i'll schedule a follow-up to pick thresholds for parallelism and decide where we gate ENI-EIP offering.
priya: thanks — drafting now and will post link.
